title: 2008 HMMT November Guts Problem 10
statement: Find the sum of all positive integers \(n\) such that \(n\) divides \(n^{2}+n+2\).

solutions.text: 3 Since \(n\) always divides \(n^{2}+n\), the only \(n\) that work are divisors of 2 , because if \(n\) divides \(a\) and \(n\) divides \(b\), then \(n\) divides \(a+b\). So the solutions are 1 and 2 which sum to 3 .
